title: Can classical theories of gravity produce entanglement?
summary: A recent paper published in Nature [Nature,646,813(2025)] claims that quantum particles become entangled through their gravitational interaction, even when the gravitational potential is classical. Here we show that the entanglement found by the authors is a consequence of letting particles diffuse from one object to the other. When this is not allowed, the wavefunction remains factorized.
